findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was a severely dented can of campbell’s soup on a shelf in the grocery section. The dents were on the side seam of the can and there was a point at the top seam. The can was pulled from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that packaging of food items are in dent free condition.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a bottle of glass cleaner stored on a shelf directly above the triple sink. Discussed with PIC and the bottle was removed. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of clean dishes.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed stagnant waste water inside of the mop sink in the back-stock area. The person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that a work order will be placed to have the sink serviced so that waste water is able to drain properly. Stagnant waste water can attract unwanted pest and insects.  Ensure that waste water is never stagnant and is able to drain in an appropriate sanitary manner.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.15 Flushing a Waste Retention Tank. A tank for liquid waste retention shall be thoroughly flushed and drained in a sanitary manner during the servicing operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Empty buckets and jugs were observed to be stored inside of the handwashing sink. Discussed with an employee and the items were removed from the sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are accessible for employees to wash hands and is only used for handwashing purposes and not for storage. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
There were several boxes of creamer stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. PIC removed the boxes from the floor and placed them onto a shelf. Ensure that food items are always stored off the ground and in a manner that prevents contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Pre-made deli sandwiches in the open air cooler were observed to not be date marked. PIC noted that the sandwiches are taken from the freezer the night before and thawed until the next morning and then placed in the cooler.  PIC was unsure on how long the sandwiches had been in the cooler. Due to the uncertainty, the sandwhich were discarded. Ensure that TCS food that are being held in a facility for longer than 24 hours are to be date marked and held in the facility for no longer than 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Boxes with single service items inside were observed to be stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Discussed with PIC and the boxes were lifted and moved onto crates.  Ensure that single service items are always off the ground and stored in a manner that prevents them from being contaminated. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items were observed for cross contamination, hot holding, date marking, and chemical storage. See violations 15, 21, 23, & 28 for details. The dispenser used for cheese and chili sauces was stocked with product available for service despite not holding proper temperature since the Friday prior per information provided during inspection. An infrared thermometer was being used to check temperatures for roller grill items, and both metal stem food thermometers were not accurate when checked for calibration. Handwashing was said to be occurring at the 3 part sink rather than the designated handwashing sink, which was apparent based on the soiled conditions of the handwashing sink. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Handwashing sink adjacent to 3 part sink was heavily soiled and didn’t look like it was used by staff at all recently. One of the managers made reference to washing their hands at the 3 part sink. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was discussed. PIC was advised to revisit proper handwashing and where to wash hands with all staff.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Empty dish detergent bottle was observed in the basin of the handwashing sink. Bottle was removed and discarded to allow for access to wash hands.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.13 Handwashing sign was posted above the 3 part sink. A manager made reference to washing their hands at the 3 part sink because it was a bigger sink. Manager removed and discarded the sign at request of inspector and was advised on handwashing at the designated handwashing sink.
All sinks not used for handwashing should not be supplied with handwashing aids/devices.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Fountain soda nozzles and diffusers were observed with varying amounts of mold buildup, with some nozzles having chunky buildup indicating a lack of cleaning for quite some time. Fountain soda machines were taken out of service. Soda nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during inspection.  
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Cheese sauce and chili sauces were observed with internal temperature of 110F and 113F for dispensed product. Chili sauce and cheese sauce were placed in the dispenser as of 6/8, and both products were removed and discarded after being wasted for inventory.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Open packages of hotdogs and smoked sausages were observed without date marks in the walk-in cooler. Exact date when products were opened was unknown. Items were wasted for inventory and discarded upon request of inspector. Ensure open packages of hotdogs and sausages are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days.
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle of pink liquid without a label was observed in the front lobby with other chemicals. PIC confirmed it was glass cleaner and placed the product in a properly labeled bottle.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-201.11 Spray bottles of Purell Food Service Sanitizer and Bathroom Tuff Stain Remover were stored on top of and next to Red Bull products in the hallway across from the walk-of cooler. Chemicals were relocated to proper storage area. 
Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles by separating toxic materials by spacing or partitioning and locating toxic materials in an area that is not above food, equipment, utensils, linens, single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Gehl’s dispenser used for chili and cheese sauces was holding around 110F and unable to maintain product at 135F. Per information provided and labels, sauces were placed in the dispenser on 6/8. PIC noted the temperature wasn’t holding correctly since the Friday prior, and a work order was placed for the machine to get checked. In the meantime, the products should have been removed and not available for service. Gehl’s dispenser is out of order until it can be repaired or replaced.
Equipment for cooling and heating food, and holding cold and hot food, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Two metal stem thermometers were reading at 60F and 70F at ambient temperature. Ice point method was used to calibrate thermometers, which were reading below 20F and below 30F when placed in ice water solution. Thermometers were calibrated to 32F. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 1) Leak was observed at the gasket of the drain plug under the sanitize basin at the 3 part sink. Sanitizer solution slowly drained from the sink when the stopper was in place. Work order was placed for repair. A flat drain cover was purchased at a nearby store to help hold solution in the basin until the drain plug can be properly repaired.
2) Handwashing sink in right restroom was observed to be slow draining. Have the sink serviced to allow for proper drainage during use.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 REPEAT 1) Floor to wall junctures along the wall beneath the handwashing sink and 3 part sink and around the mopsink were without base coving. Properly seal the floors to wall junctures.
2) Wall trim was loose and lower portion of wall covering was bowing at the chemical storage shelving to the right of the mopsink. Provide proper repairs to seal the area in question. 
3) Floor tiles in both restrooms were cracked in multiple places. Work on resealing the tiles to provide smooth, easily cleanable surface.
4) Wall tile was missing by the clean-out next to the toilet in the right restroom, and a hole was observed at the corner by the floor. Provide proper repairs.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Floor in back storage area was in need of cleaning under storage shelves, especially along the walls.
2) Handwashing sink next to 3 part sink was heavily soiled in the basin with buildup and chunky debris. Sink was cleaned during inspection.
3) Mopsink was observed to be heavily soiled with buildup, and the basin was black from dirt and lack of cleaning. Mopsink was cleaned during inspection.
4) Floor drain under the 3 part sink and cover were heavily soiled with buildup. Clean the floor drain and the cover.
5) Floor, wall and attached plumbing under the 3 part sink were soiled with general buildup and dust. Clean the aforementioned surfaces under the 3 part sink.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sanitizer bucket to have 0ppm of quaternary ammonium. Quaternary ammonium concentrations must be maintained between 200ppm and 400ppm or as directed by the manufacturer’s label. The sani bucket was changed during the inspection.  

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Windshield wiper fluid was observed stored above candy and other food in the dry storage area. Chemicals must be stored below food so there is no risk of contamination in the event of a spill. The windshield wiper fluid was moved during the inspection. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Ceiling tiles in the bathrooms and above the soda syrup and 3 part sink are acoustic ceiling tiles. These are not smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable. Ensure ceiling tiles are replaced with ceiling tiles that are smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable. Additionally, the wall behind the soda syrup is not smooth and non-absorbent. Ensure the wall is made smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Floor and wall junctures near the 3 part sink and the mop sink were not sealed and/or coved. Ensure the floor-wall junctures are properly sealed. 

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed broken cans inside the hand sink. The drinks were placed in the sink because they were leaking. The hand sink may only be used for hand washing only. Drinks may be dumped or placed in a utility or prep sink if need be. The drinks were moved during the inspection to correct the violation., 
(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed black mold/mildew starting to build up in the ice dispenser of the soda fountain. Ensure this surface is cleaned regularly to maintain clean. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The PIC stated that he was a Certified Food Manager, but could not find his certificate. Ensure that the certificate is available during the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed no date marking on a package of opened hot dogs. Ensure that all foods opened and not used within 24 hours are properly date marked. PIC date marked to pack of hot dogs.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test strips for bleach were not available during the inspection. Ensure test strips are ordered and available to test the concentration of bleach solutions. PIC stated he would order test strips.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13 (A) (C) Observed no caulking or coving on the wall across from the restrooms. Ensure that caulking or coving is installed to seal the floor to the wall.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Fans in walk in cooler covered with debris

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Hand sinks in men's and women's restrooms slow to drain.

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed pre-packaged muffins and people chow to not be properly labeled with the ingredients or allergens. All foods packaged in advance of retail sale must have proper labeling.
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed raw wood on the side of the new cabinets next to the door leading to the back room. Seal or paint raw wood.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sinks in the restrooms to be slow draining. Repair plumbing so sinks drain effectively.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed water pooling on the floor near the three compartment sink. Apparently the roof is in need of repair and is scheduled to occur. In the meantime, keep floors clean and dry.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Lights in the back area over food storage and dish washing areas are not shielded. Provide light shields or shatterproof bulbs.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a couple chemical spray bottles and a container of bowl cleaner to be stored on the shelf immediately inside the door to the back room above Gehl's cheese sauce and single service items. Cleaners were moved to the chemical storage area near the three compartment sink during the inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a couple packages of hot dogs, brats and roller grill items that were open and not labeled with the date that the packages were opened. These items were discarded during inspection and it was discussed that these items must be date marked and held no longer than 7 days maximum (facility records discard dates on all products).
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed raw wood on the side of the new cabinets next to the door leading to the back room. Seal or paint raw wood.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the container holding the large coffee filters to be soiled with an accumulation of debris in the bottom. 2) Observed the bucket underneath the ice chute in the back to be soiled inside. 3) Observed the cookie trays to have some accumulation of baked food on them. Wash, rinse and sanitize these food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelves in the walk in cooler to be soiled with mold and dust accumulation. Clean the shelves.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed the coffee filters to be uncovered next to the coffee maker. Store coffee filters covered and protected from potential contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the area around the floor drain underneath the three compartment sink to be soiled. Clean the floor drain.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a spray bottle with a green liquid in it on the back storage shelf to not be labeled with the name of the contents. Label all chemicals with the name of the contents. Spray bottle was labeled during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed coffee filters sitting on top of the International Delight machine unprotected. Store coffee filters in a covered container to protect them from potential contamination.
750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed several areas ( the insides of the holes for wiring and hoses, the edge along the side nearest the walk in cooler)  with bare wood exposed on the center island. The new counter top is on order and should be installed in the next couple weeks.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a box of single service cups and a box of single service donut boxes stored on the floor in the back room. Store all single service items at least 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed a couple ceiling tiles in the back to be missing or askew. Replace ceiling tiles. 2) Observed the new ceiling tiles over the beverage machines and over the island with the roller grills to be made of non-absorbent material, however, they are not completely smooth and have deep pockets in them that would make it hard to clean. It was discussed that these should be smooth like the tiles the lights are hung from, and maintenance was on site and said he could have this fixed. 3) Observed a trim piece to be separated from the wall in the hallway leading to the walk in cooler.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a package of hot dogs and a bag of half and half in the walk in cooler to not be date marked. Date mark all potentially hazardous foods and hold not to exceed 7 days.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed an ice scoop being stored within an ice scoop with the handle of the inner scoop in contact with the food contact surface of the outer scoop. Store utensils to be protected from potential contamination. CORRECTED> Observed tornadoes being stored in a shopping bag. Store food in food grade containers. Torndadoes were voluntarily discarded.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
2ND REPEAT> Observed the cabinets beneath the self serve soda and coffee machines to be in minor disrepair with shelves having exposed particle board and edges on counter top peeling away exposing particle board. Repair, seal or replace items that are not smooth and easily cleanable. NEW> Observed the ice machine to have a seal in disrepair. Replace seal on ice bin.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Facility states they are not using sanitizer to wash utensils or clean surfaces and use only dish soap for utensil washing and cleaning surfaces. Facility has chlorine and test strips available, however, they are not using them. Inspectors discussed proper wash, rinse and santize sequencing for utensil washing and proper sanitizer bucket or spray bottle preparation for sanitizing surfaces. A wash, rinse, sanitize handout was left with facility.
750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ice spouts on the Pepsi fountain machine to be soiled. Wash, rinse and sanitize ice spouts.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1)REPEAT> the cabinet beneath the self serve coffee and soda area. 2) the upper lid on the ice machine bin soiled with rust, 3) between the Pepsi soda fountain and cup dispenser soiled with larger debris. Clean non-food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the following leaks: 1) in the back storage area, possibly the walk-in condenser is leaking onto the floor, 2) the Pibb nozzle on the soda fountain is leaking. Pepsi has been called and will have repairman on site within 4 hours.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
3RD REPEAT> Observed multiple ceiling tiles that are askew, missing, have holes or have water damage throughout the facility. Repair or replace ceiling tiles so that they are smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed dirty mop water sitting in the mop bucket while not in use. Dispose of dirty mop water after use to prevent harborage.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed 8 hot dogs and 6 tornados on roller 1 to be at an internal temperature of 119 degrees F. Items were checked with a stem thermometer. All items were voluntarily discarded.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
REPEAT > 1)Observed the cabinets beneath the self serve soda and coffee machines to be in minor disrepair with shelves having exposed particle board and edges on counter top peeling away exposing particle board. Repair, seal, or replace items that are not smooth and easily cleanable.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > No test kit for chlorine sanitizer was present at the facility. Test kit was provided during inspection.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
REPEAT > The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: 1) The cabinet beneath the self serve coffee and soda area. 2) The storage shelves in the backroom. 3) The shelving units in the walk-in cooler. Clean there areas.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment:
Observed hose connected to the mop sink faucet without back flow prevention present. Hose was removed and back flow preventer was ordered during inspection.
750-1080 The potable water system shall be installed to preclude the possibility of backflow.  Devices to protect against backflow and back siphonage shall be installed at all fixtures and equipment where an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water inlet is not provided between the water outlet from the fixture and the fixture’s flood-level rim and wherever else backflow or backsiphonage may occur. Install backflow prevention device.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > No paper towels were observed at the backroom hand sink. Paper towels were provided during inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
1) 2ND REPEAT> The corner by the ice machine has coving in disrepair due to previous pest problems ( Currently no new evidence of pests). The coving around the ice machine is in disrepair. Repair coving and holes in the coving so coving is smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.
2) The floors were observed to be soiled in the back room along the walls and below shelving and equipment. Clean the floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
2ND REPEAT > 1) There remains multiple ceiling tiles that are askew, missing, have holes, or have water damage, Repair or replace ceiling tiles so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
2) The trim along the door next to ice machine is broken and missing exposing the edges of dry wall. Repair or replace trim so it is easily cleanable.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed three bottles of cleaner being stored above the three pan sink on a wire rack. Items were moved to permitted location during inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment:
Observed one spray bottle of cleaner to be unlabeled net to the self serve coffee station. Bottle was labeled with name of contents.
750-1300 Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a FSSMC employee.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.
